#Third_Imposed_War #Presence_in_International_Media #Elite_Diplomacy_in_War 81 #International🔰 Iran-Oman Agreement: A Step Toward Joint Management, Not Full Reopening of the Strait👤Seyed Mohammad Sadegh Emamian, faculty member of Amirkabir University and co-founder of the Sharif Governance Think Tank, in an interview with CGTN at the think tank's premises on August 18, addressed the distinction between the recent bilateral negotiations and the broader issue of the Strait of Hormuz:🔹If finalized, the Iran-Oman agreement will be a constructive and preliminary step toward joint management or governance of the Strait of Hormuz.🔸However, these bilateral arrangements must be clearly distinguished from the full reopening of the strait. These are two separate matters: one between Iran and Oman, and the other between Iran and the United States.🔹The United States remains an aggressor that has imposed an unprovoked war on Iran. Until the conditions for ending hostilities are met, the full reopening of the strait will remain contingent on broader political and security developments.📌Watch the full interview here.💠 Sharif Governance Think Tank |Website| |Telegram Channel| |Bale Channel| |Rubika Channel| |Instagram|

#Third_Imposed_War#Presence_in_International_Media#International🔰Iran, relying on the approach of endogenous security and the idea of a strong region, has a functionalist approach to the Mecca Agreement👤Mohammad Amin Hazrati, senior researcher at the Center for Elite Diplomacy of the think tank, in an interview with Pakistan's Asia One network on August 10, has explained Iran's approach to the agreement between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan:🔹The explicit message of Iran's recent stance to its neighbors is a fundamental critique of the imported security model. The presence of extra-regional forces not only does not guarantee stability, but itself becomes a focal point for escalating crises.🔸Tehran's approach to the Mecca security pact is based on strategic intelligence and preventing the formation of an anti-Iranian security architecture. Instead of hasty confrontation, Iran evaluates the nature of this pact based on its objective performance.🔹From Tehran's perspective, if this cooperation leads to increased strategic autonomy of regional powers and does not become part of American aggressive plans, it can have a defensive function.🔸The pattern governing the future of relations among regional countries is competitive coexistence.💠Sharif Governance Think Tank|Website| |Telegram Channel| |Bale Channel| |Rubika Channel| |Instagram|

#Expert_Opinion 775#Regulation🔰The Slaughter of the Concept of Regulation🔍Amirhossein Ghalandari, senior researcher at the Regulation Group, has written a note about the recent ruling of the General Assembly of the Administrative Court of Justice regarding the annulment of Resolution 473 of the Competition Council:🔹The recent ruling of the General Assembly of the Administrative Court of Justice regarding the annulment of Resolution 473 of the Competition Council appears to be a legal dispute in the automobile market; but behind it lies a bigger question: What has happened to regulation in Iran's governance system? The issue is not just a resolution or an institution, but the position that regulation has not yet found in the country.🔸Regulation came to create stability, but in Iran, the regulator's authority is unstable; it came for impartial arbitration, but role conflicts persist; it came to curb market power, but it lacks resources itself; and it came for expert decision-making, but its decisions are subject to political and institutional interventions. When we strip regulation of these characteristics, the issue is no longer a few scattered dysfunctions; the issue is the slaughter of the very concept of regulation.📌Read the full text on the think tank's website. 🗞️Published in: Farhikhtegan newspaper💠Sharif Governance Think Tank |Website| |Telegram Channel| |Bale Channel| |Rubika Channel| |Instagram|

#Third_Imposed_War #Presence_in_International_Media #International🔰Trump's escalating economic pressure aimed at extracting concessions and reopening the strait will not yield results👤Mohammad Amin Hezrati, senior researcher at the Think Tank's Elite Diplomacy Center, in an interview with Qatar's Al-Arabi network on August 10, examined the quality of Iran-Oman negotiations regarding the Strait of Hormuz and the nature of America's focus on economic pressure against Iran:🔹An examination of the Iran-Oman negotiation process indicates Tehran's strategic transition from viewing the Strait of Hormuz as a hidden power tool toward institutionalizing its leverage. 🔸Tehran no longer sees the Strait of Hormuz merely as a deterrence tool; rather, it is attempting to convert its geopolitical weight and field power into sustainable legal and political arrangements.🔹The main goal is to prevent a return to the status quo and to transform geopolitical influence into tangible rights, balance in economic exploitation, and consolidate Iran's sovereign role in the new structure of the strait.🔸Washington's shift in tactics from military confrontation to economic pressure tools symbolizes "coercive diplomacy" to reduce costs.💠Sharif Governance Think Tank|Website| |Telegram Channel| |Bale Channel| |Rubika Channel| |Instagram|

Iran has been the target of two rounds of unprovoked aggression by Israel and the United States, which has resulted in heavy civilian costs, including the deaths of hundreds of students.🔸Although political relations between the governments of Tehran and Baku have generally been positive, there was an expectation of a more explicit political stance in support of Iran's national sovereignty and condemnation of the aggressors from the northern neighbors during the recent conflict; a stance that was more clearly expressed by some other neighbors such as Iraq and Pakistan.🔹Recent incidents, including the attack on Iranian ships, showed the absence of strong public condemnation and reinforced historical patterns of mistrust.💠Sharif Governance Think Tank |Website| |Telegram Channel| |Bale Channel| |Rubika Channel| |Instagram|

#Third_Imposed_War#Presence_in_International_Media#International🔰Contradictory Messages and Efforts to Strike a Balance in the Strait of Hormuz👤Ali Salehian, Director of the Elite Diplomacy Center at the Think Tank, said in an interview with Pakistan's Asia One network on August 5:🔹Trump's public statements about negotiations should be seen primarily as messaging aimed at his domestic MAGA audience. In practice, both sides are simultaneously pursuing military and diplomatic paths to reach an acceptable balance.🔸For Iran, the priority is clear: consolidating sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz. This is a security issue rooted in the experience of the February 28 war, not a financial or commercial matter.🔹US threats of more severe military action are unlikely to change Iran's strategy. Tehran faces what it considers an existential threat and is prepared to bear significant costs to protect its national security and sovereignty.🔸The US, in contrast, lacks low-cost military options. A ground operation, an attack on energy, or an attempt to force the reopening of the strait would trigger retaliatory responses from Iran at the regional level.💠Sharif Governance Think Tank|Website| |Telegram Channel| |Bale Channel| |Rubika Channel| |Instagram|
